title: MiniMax H3 official Hugging Face model card
claims: H3-Base-FL2VA and H3-Base-Ref2VA are separate task-specific BF16 checkpoints.
FL2VA supports text-to-audio-video and first/last-frame-to-audio-video with zero, one, or two images; Ref2VA supports reference images, videos, and audio.
The released Base checkpoints are CFG-distilled Omni Transformer weights.

Ref2VA limits are at most 9 images, 3 video clips, 3 audio clips, 15 seconds total per video/audio category, and 12 mixed files; output is 24 FPS, 32 kHz stereo, 4–15 seconds, with 768-pixel short edge by default.

resources.resolution: 768p Base default short edge; 2K through H3-Regenerate-2K API
resources.workflow: MiniMax H3 Base FL2VA or Ref2VA local deployment

limitations: The card does not report single-GPU L4 or A100 host-RAM, VRAM-peak, or end-to-end timing; H3-Regenerate-2K is not open-sourced.

title: Hugging Face Diffusers MiniMax-H3 ModularPipeline source
claims: Video and audio schedulers use shifts 12.0 and 3.0 inside one transformer call per denoise step.
Guidance is baked into the weights; the pipeline has no guider, negative_prompt, or guidance_scale, and every denoise step runs exactly one forward pass.
The pipeline exposes t2va, fl2va, and ref2va workflows over the corresponding transformer partitions.
The Ref2VA blocks state that audio references cannot be the only references.

resources.steps: N denoise steps = N transformer forwards in this pipeline

limitations: This source does not provide the Base default step count or hardware benchmark; sigma-point conventions may differ in wrappers.

title: DiffSynth-Studio MiniMax-H3 documentation
claims: The NF4 quick start enables VRAM management and states a minimum of 7GB VRAM for that path.
The example uses 480x832, 124 frames, 50 inference steps, and BF16 computation with CPU offload configuration.
The MiniMaxH3Pipeline interface defaults to 768x1344, 124 frames, 50 inference steps, cfg_scale 1.0, video flow_shift 12.0, audio_flow_shift 3.0, and tiled VAE true with tile size 256 and overlap 64.
The documentation states negative_prompt has no effect by default because the model is CFG-distilled; video and audio use independent sigma schedules.

resources.precision: BF16 compute with NF4 quantized components in quick start
resources.workflow: DiffSynth MiniMaxH3Pipeline with VRAM management and CPU offload

limitations: The 7GB value is a framework minimum declaration, not a complete L4 benchmark; no host-RAM, peak-memory, or wall-time measurement is supplied.

title: Comfy-Org native MiniMax H3 workflows
claims: Native T2V/I2V workflows use the FL2VA model; R2V uses the separate Ref2VA model.
The native T2V/I2V workflow defaults to 20 steps; turbo_mode uses the FL2VA 8-step Lightning LoRA with default turbo strength 1.0.
The native R2V workflow defaults to 20 steps and its optional Lightning LoRA is Ref2VA 4-step; the page describes slightly lower audio and motion quality in turbo mode.
R2V supports at most 9 images, 3 videos, and 3 standalone audio clips; match and max reference resize modes are documented.

resources.steps: 20 Base default; 8 FL2VA turbo; 4 Ref2VA turbo
resources.precision: INT8 ConvRot DiT, NVFP4-AWQ text encoder, INT8 ConvRot video VAE, FP32 audio VAE in storage example

limitations: The quality description is workflow documentation, not a controlled benchmark or identity-retention score; host RAM and L4/A100 timing are absent.

title: ModelTC Minimax-H3-Turbo model specifications
claims: The author table lists FL2VA 4-step v0.1 at 544p with shifts 12/3 and 4 NFE; FL2VA 8-step v1.0 at 544p with shifts 12/3 and 8 NFE; FL2VA 4/8-step v1.0 768p at 1344x768 with shifts 6/3; and Ref2VA 4-step v0.1 at 544p with shifts 12/3.
The table marks FL2VA 8-step v1.0 recommended inference as 8 or 4 NFE, while the other listed variants use their trained NFE.
The repository's ComfyUI graphs default T2VA/I2VA to FL2VA 8-step v1.0 and Ref2VA to Ref2VA 4-step v0.1.
The repository gives a four-NFE sigma example and states its distilled reference-image training uses match resize.

resources.precision: BF16 LoRA artifacts plus matching H3 base

limitations: The table defines adapter contracts but does not provide L4/A100 memory or controlled quality measurements.

title: vLLM-Omni MiniMax-H3 Turbo recipe
claims: The recipe table lists FL2VA 4-step artifacts with 4 forwards and num_inference_steps 5, and FL2VA 8-step artifacts with 8 forwards and num_inference_steps 9.
544p artifacts use flow_shift 12; 768p artifacts use flow_shift 6; audio_flow_shift is 3 across the listed family.
Requests are validated against the loaded artifact's task, step, and shift contract; mismatches are rejected rather than silently accepted.
Ref2VA rows require a separate ref2va server/task and are not served by the FL2VA command.

resources.steps: 4/8 denoiser forwards; wrapper request uses 5/9 sigma points
resources.workflow: vLLM-Omni H3 server with FL2VA or Ref2VA task

limitations: No L4/A100 host-RAM benchmark is reported; request-step and forward-step conventions are specific to this recipe.

title: Video Rebirth HyperFlow for MiniMax-H3
claims: HyperFlow is an 8-step LoRA obtained by data-free flow self-distillation.
The official H3 base weights, VAEs, conditioner, and t2va/fl2va/ref2va workflows remain in use; only the LoRA and loader are added.
The adapter is rank 256/alpha 256 over 316 modules and is about 2.8GB; its fixed sigma grid uses video/audio shifts 12/3.
The source states the standard Diffusers 50-point schedule performs 49 model forwards while HyperFlow performs 8; HyperFlow takes the step count from the weights file instead of num_inference_steps.
The dedicated load_hyperflow_lora loader installs HyperFlow's TwoTimeEmbedder and endpoint-time keys; the README says it is not a generic LoRA for diffusers load_lora_adapter.

resources.gpu: 1 GPU auto CPU-offload recipe; optional Ulysses up to 4 GPUs
resources.workflow: Official Diffusers ModularPipeline t2va/fl2va/ref2va with HyperFlow loader

limitations: The 24GB reserve margin mentioned by the source was validated on H200, not L4; its 49-forward wording is a sigma-point convention and should not overwrite DiffSynth's separate implementation loop evidence. The adapter requires the dedicated HyperFlow loader rather than generic LoRA loading.

title: drbaph MiniMax-H3 Turbo LoRAs for ComfyUI
claims: HyperFlow conversions are attributed to Video Rebirth; LightX2V files are Dynamic-SVD resizes of named official LightX2V FL2V/Ref2V artifacts.

The current v4 step-600 EMA pruned workflow uses 6–8 steps, Euler, Beta, strength 1.0, video shift 12, and audio shift 4–6; the author labels 8 steps for quality/motion/audio stability and 4 steps for matching LightX2V FL2V/Ref2V workflows.
The LightX2V resized files use an average projection rank of 21.724359; the card explicitly says weight-reconstruction similarity is not a perceptual video-quality score.

Pruned compatibility conversions remove 51 AdaLN pairs because their dimensions do not match the pruned/curve-form base; the author says these conversions should not be assumed identical to the original full-model LoRA.

resources.resolution: 768p for named v1.1 FL2V files; other variants not uniformly specified

limitations: No controlled L4/A100 benchmark; community conversions have base-model compatibility constraints and author-described experimental variants.

title: Alibaba PAI MiniMax-H3 Acc LoRAs
claims: The model card describes Parallel Decoding Distillation (PDD) applied to MiniMax-H3 for few-step generation.
It publishes one BF16 rank-64/network-alpha-64 Acc LoRA for FL2VA and one matching Acc LoRA for Ref2VA, both named 8Step.
The card's demo table compares each Acc adapter with Base and MiniMax-H3-Turbo 4-step examples at LoRA weight 1.0.
The quick-start scripts use Diffusers MiniMax-H3 ModularPipeline and derive the required inference steps from the adapter configuration.
The PDD loading path uses apply_pdd_lora and requires diffusers >= 0.40.0.

resources.resolution: 768p demo for FL2VA; Ref2VA demo resolution not specified in card text
resources.workflow: VideoX-Fun / Diffusers ModularPipeline FL2VA or Ref2VA

limitations: The card does not report L4/A100 memory, RAM, wall time, or an independent quality evaluation; it is a matching-base adapter rather than a standalone base checkpoint. A generic single-LoRA loader cannot be assumed to install its PDD head bank; use the documented apply_pdd_lora path.

title: smhfacct MiniMax H3 FL2VA/Ref2VA hybrid models
claims: The variants are created from official pruned INT8-ConvRot FL2VA and Ref2VA checkpoints by tensor-level weight selection, with FL2VA as the base and later-block Ref2VA adaln_proj ranges b15–49, b20–49, b25–49, or b30–49.
The author says no additional training, fine-tuning, or gradient optimization was performed.
The model card assigns b30–49 closer to FL2VA and b20–49 closer to Ref2VA, describing a gradual subjective tradeoff between raw visual/audio quality and reference capability.
The intended tasks are text/image/video/audio-to-video reference workflows; the card warns that results vary by prompt, reference type, and settings.

resources.workflow: Ref2VA-style reference-conditioned workflow with merged FL2VA base

limitations: This is an experimental subjective merge; no independent reproduction, identity metric, audio metric, or L4/A100 benchmark was supplied.

title: Kijai MiniMax-H3-experimental
claims: The card describes its ref LoRA as the difference between FL2VA and Ref2VA and explicitly calls it completely experimental with unknown use case.
Its PDMD LoRAs were converted and rank-reduced from pdmd2026 2NFE and 4NFE LoRAs; its DMAD LoRA links to ZhengmingYu/DMAD.
The card lists W4A8 and W6A8 formats, requires ComfyUI 0.31.0, and says int8-convrot VAE needs ComfyUI 0.36.0 for maximum speed benefit.
The card reports an int8-convrot light VAE as about 1.3x faster for decoding, while the ref LoRA task utility remains unconfirmed.

resources.steps: PDMD source files 2/4 NFE; other experimental files unspecified
resources.precision: W4A8/W6A8 experimental weights plus BF16 LoRAs

limitations: No identity/audio quality, task success, L4/A100 memory, or timing evidence; the author explicitly marks the ref LoRA use case unknown.

title: NVIDIA SANA Sol Engine MiniMax-H3 DataCenter benchmark
claims: The page benchmarks 4x A100 SM80 using the original BF16 checkpoint with no model offload, Ulysses-4, warm batch 1, 1344x768, 124 frames, and 50 steps.
Dense end-to-end time is 217.32 seconds and full-opt time is 61.28 seconds on 4x A100; full-opt peak memory is 49,126 MiB per A100.
The full-opt path uses Triton SM80 Sol-Attn; the page reports generated audio with every clip.

resources.workflow: SANA Sol Engine full-opt, Ulysses-4, no model offload

limitations: The source does not state whether the A100 nodes are 40GB or 80GB and does not report host RAM; this is a 4-GPU high-resource benchmark, not a single-A100 or L4 result.

title: zenryokukikai MiniMax-H3 WebUI GPU measurements
claims: At 864x480, 20 steps, 124 frames (5.17 seconds), the author reports A100 80GB with INT8 ConvRot and Triton at 4.25 seconds per iteration and 110 seconds total.
The same repo reports 16.9 seconds per iteration for 1344x768 under its A100 80GB INT8 ConvRot setup.

resources.workflow: ComfyUI native with comfy-kitchen Triton backend

limitations: No host-RAM value, stage breakdown, warm/cold qualification, or controlled Base/Turbo quality comparison is given.

title: Marwanto606 Modal A100-80GB ComfyUI case
claims: The author reports a Modal A100-80GB with 1TB RAM running ComfyUI MiniMax-H3 T2V at 960x544 for 10 seconds.
The reported usage is 50.62GB VRAM, 100.8GB RAM, and 307.08 seconds generation time.
The listed stack includes pruned INT8 ConvRot diffusion, NVFP4 Qwen text encoder, video/audio VAE files, and a Turbo LoRA.

resources.precision: INT8 ConvRot diffusion, NVFP4 text encoder, VAE files and Turbo LoRA as listed

limitations: The author says time varies with prompt; steps, seed, warm/cold state, and stage timing are not specified, so this is a single first-hand case rather than a controlled benchmark.

title: ComfyUI MiniMax-H3 L4 workflows
claims: The repository is preconfigured for NVIDIA L4 24GB VRAM and 32GB RAM with INT8 quantization and NVFP4 text encoding.

Its table reports native 15–20-step T2V/I2V at about 3.5–4.5 minutes, native R2V at 4–5 minutes, Turbo 6-step T2V/I2V at 2.5–3 minutes, Turbo 6-step R2V at 3–4 minutes, and unaccelerated 20-step T2V at 12–15 minutes.
The repository includes separate T2V, I2V, and R2V workflow JSON files for native and Turbo paths.

resources.time_s: 210–270 native T2V/I2V; 240–300 native R2V; 150–180 Turbo T2V/I2V; 180–240 Turbo R2V; 720–900 baseline
resources.precision: INT8 diffusion and NVFP4 text encoder
resources.workflow: ComfyUI custom SpeedStack and Turbo workflows

limitations: The table omits resolution, frame count, seed, warm/cold state, I/O breakdown, and independent quality checks; the repository also contains NSFW-specific workflows, which are outside this report's claims.

title: MiniMax-AI awesome integration index
claims: The index lists a 24GB-card starting stack of pruned INT8 ConvRot DiT 19.53GiB plus NVFP4-AWQ text encoder 14.61GiB.
It lists the original MiniMaxAI repository at 464.2GiB total, with each original transformer partition at 61.73GiB, and marks DiffSynth NF4 path at an 8GB VRAM floor.
The index states FL2VA typically has higher raw output while Ref2VA accepts more reference material with lower base quality, and that Ref Patch can partially bridge the gap.

resources.gpu: 24GB class card; exact GPU not fixed
resources.precision: Pruned INT8 ConvRot DiT + NVFP4-AWQ text encoder

limitations: This is a first-party curated index, not a benchmark; component file sizes are disk sizes, not peak VRAM or host-RAM measurements, and the FL2VA/Ref2VA quality wording has no score table.
